chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is an oath in the disobedience of Allah and in severing ties of kinship.
ai.seo_question: Is an oath to disobey God or cut off family ties considered valid and binding in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that an oath remains legally binding even when taken to perform a sinful act, such as disobeying Allah or severing family ties (qati'at al-rahim), rather than being voided by the sin itself. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the principle that the validity of the oath (yamin) is distinct from the moral status of the act sworn upon, requiring the swearer to fulfill the obligation or pay expiation (kaffarah) if they break it. It highlights the practical legal weight of the oath as a binding contract in personal status law.
